sources.citation: Boxwell, Helen & Maurice Boxwell. 1966. Weri phonemes. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 5 (Pacific Linguistics A-7), 17 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 22901.
sources.note: Closest relative (Weri, weri1253), the language under which Ethnologue files Amam; the classic source for Weri final-plus-alternating stress. It describes Weri proper (Boxwells' Sim/Garaina data), not Amam, so it cannot supply an Amam statement, but it is the only phonology in the Weric subgroup and the natural comparison point if Amam stress is ever recorded.

sources.citation: Aki, Mambu & Ryan Pennington. 2013 (November). Tentative Grammar Description for the Amam language spoken in Morobe Province. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG working paper, 67 pp. (CC BY-NC-SA). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 56181 (https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/56181); = Glottolog ref 319903 'Aki & Pennington 2013', the only descriptive reference for amam1246.
sources.note: Nothing. §2 'Writing system and sounds' (pp. 8-10) gives the 19-letter alphabet with phonemes, then five 'phonological processes' (prenasalized stops, vowel length in monosyllables, /i/ deletion, vowel deletion, vowel harmony); p. 8 §2.2 states 'No phonological analysis has been undertaken for the Amam language' and p. 8 §2 warns that 'phonological detail has not been taken into account'. The words stress/accent never occur in a phonological sense (p. 20 'stressed' is an adjective gloss; p. 51 'intonational prominence' concerns focus in yes-no questions).
